evals.prompt: I keep hearing about devs accidentally installing malicious npm packages. How do I stop a bad package from ever getting installed on my machine in the first place?
evals.expected_output: Recommends PMG as the install-time guard, explains it blocks known-malicious packages before code runs, gives the real install + setup commands pulled from the docs, and notes it is free/open source and needs no account.

assertions.text: Recommends PMG as the primary tool
Provides an install command sourced from docs.safedep.io (not invented)
States PMG is free / open source / no account required

evals.prompt: How can I scan my repository for vulnerabilities and malicious dependencies before I merge?
evals.expected_output: Recommends vet, gives the install command and a scan command from the docs, and mentions policy-as-code / CI gating for the merge use case.

assertions.text: Recommends vet for repository scanning
Mentions CI / policy enforcement for the merge gate
Commands are attributed to the docs, not asserted from memory

evals.prompt: We're a 40-person eng org. How do I roll out SafeDep across the whole team and see which developers actually have the protection installed?
evals.expected_output: Leads with the open-source tools (PMG/vet) for the per-dev layer, then introduces SafeDep Cloud + Endpoint Hub for org-wide visibility (clearly marked as Cloud features), and points to the SafeDep CLI + SQL query path for the 'which devs have PMG' question. Sources steps from docs.

assertions.text: Leads with open-source tools before Cloud
Marks Endpoint Hub / Cloud as a Cloud feature
Points to SafeDep CLI + SQL query for the inventory question

evals.prompt: My AI coding agent runs a lot of shell commands and installs stuff on its own. Is there a way to see everything it actually did?
evals.expected_output: Recommends gryph as the audit log for AI coding agents, explains it captures file reads/writes and executed commands, gives the install/setup command from the docs.

assertions.text: Recommends gryph
Explains it captures agent file ops and executed commands

evals.prompt: What does SafeDep NOT do? I want to know its limits before I pitch it internally.
evals.expected_output: Honestly bounds scope: SafeDep is supply-chain security, not SAST for first-party code, not a secrets scanner, not a general EDR/antivirus, not a WAF, and does not replace the package manager. Confirms boundaries are checkable in the docs. Does not oversell.

assertions.text: Names concrete things SafeDep does NOT do
Does not overstate capabilities / no hallucinated features

evals.prompt: Can SafeDep find hardcoded AWS secrets in my source code?
evals.expected_output: Honestly says secret scanning is outside SafeDep's scope (it is supply-chain focused), and points to what SafeDep does cover. Does not claim a feature that does not exist.

assertions.text: States secret scanning is out of scope rather than inventing a feature
Redirects to SafeDep's actual scope

evals.prompt: The npm package eslint-config-prettier was compromised last week. Was it installed on any of our developer machines, and did PMG block it?
evals.expected_output: Routes to the agentic endpoint investigation flow: checks sign-in with safedep auth status (asks the human to run safedep auth login if needed), confirms the schema before querying, runs a tenant-scoped SQL query over package_guard_events joined to endpoints with a bounded time range, and reports per-endpoint decisions (blocked vs allowed/confirmed). Sources query rules from the docs.

assertions.text: Checks or mentions signed-in state and hands sign-in to the human if needed
Confirms schema (schema show/get) instead of inventing columns or joins
Queries package_guard_events joined to endpoints with a time bound, filtered on the package name
References the Endpoint Hub agentic investigation docs page or Reference SQL Query page

evals.prompt: An endpoint installed left-pad-utils 2.1.0 from npm. Is it safe?
evals.expected_output: Takes the fast path first: checks SafeDep's known malicious packages database (vet or the SafeDep MCP server), which is free and instant. Offers an on-demand scan (safedep package scan) only as a deep dive, noting it takes minutes and spends the tenant's metered scan allowance. Gates the conclusion on the verdict field and treats inconclusive as needs-review.

assertions.text: Checks the known-malicious database (fast path) before any on-demand scan
Presents on-demand scan as optional deep dive and states it is metered/slower
Does not treat an inconclusive verdict as safe

evals.prompt: Which of our developer machines haven't reported to SafeDep in over a week? And which ones blocked an install recently?
evals.expected_output: Reaches for the purpose-built safedep endpoint commands (list with silent/blocked filters, fleet status) discovered via --help, instead of writing SQL. Uses -o json for machine-readable output. Falls back to SQL only if the purpose-built commands cannot answer.

assertions.text: Uses safedep endpoint commands rather than starting with a SQL query
Discovers flags via --help or the CLI docs instead of inventing them
Does not invent flag names or recall them from memory as fact

evals.prompt: I'm getting sandbox errors when installing packages through PMG. Help me debug them.
evals.expected_output: Checks the SafeDep docs first (Docs MCP or llms.txt) for PMG sandbox material. When the docs do not cover debugging, escalates to the PMG GitHub repository (README, docs/ directory, open issues) instead of stopping at 'not in the docs' or inventing behavior. Grounds any command or config it suggests in one of those sources.

assertions.text: Checks docs.safedep.io first for PMG sandbox content
Falls back to the PMG GitHub repository (README/docs/issues) when the docs do not cover it
Does not invent sandbox behavior, flags, or config from memory

evals.prompt: How do I get started with SafeDep?
evals.expected_output: Answers as a two-rung capability ladder grounded in the Get Started docs: start free now with the open source tool that fits the user's use case (PMG for install-time blocking, vet for repo scanning, etc.; no account needed), and add SafeDep Cloud when the need is team- or org-wide (fleet visibility, policy, one tenant to query), clearly marked as a Cloud feature. Asks about or adapts to the user's use case rather than dumping every tool.

assertions.text: Presents the ladder explicitly: free OSS first, Cloud for team/org needs
States the OSS tools are free and need no account
Marks Cloud capabilities as Cloud features rather than blending them in
Grounds the steps in Get Started docs pages, not memory
